findings.headline: Early‑race stress high on fresh Mediums but no pace hit – monitor mental load
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 88.8 on lap 2 (the only in‑race reading) while the driver was on fresh Medium tyres (age 2) in dry conditions, holding P12 with a 0.4 s gap and DRS enabled. The high stress coincided with a +0.000 s pace delta, indicating no immediate pace loss, but the driver’s tone (Tired) suggests early‑race mental load that could affect later performance if not managed.

findings.headline: Mediums struggled on wet; Intermediates recovered lap time
findings.detail: When the wet track began (lap 19) the Medium tyres showed a +9.296 s pace delta, a clear loss of grip. Switching to Intermediates at lap 28 reduced the delta to –1.503 s by lap 29, confirming the tyre change restored performance despite the wet surface.

findings.headline: Third Medium stint shows stable pace despite modelled degradation
findings.detail: During the second Medium stint (laps 39‑52) the modelled degradation was –0.086 s/lap, yet pace delta stayed around 0 s until lap 45 when a brief wet patch returned (+0.172 s). The driver maintained consistent pace on dry‑track laps 40‑44, indicating the tyre model is reliable for predicting performance on a drying circuit.

findings.headline: High stress reading at lap 52 did not affect pace – sample too small
findings.detail: The only post‑race stress reading (9.7) is from a non‑racing lap and should not be used to assess in‑race fatigue; however, the deterministic strategy call at lap 52 notes stress 89/100 with no performance loss, suggesting the driver can tolerate high stress without pace degradation, but the sample size is too small to generalise.
evidence: strategy call: Stress 89/100 but pace trend -0.01s/lap

findings.headline: Blue‑flag periods did not impact lap time
findings.detail: Blue flags appeared from lap 21 onward while on Mediums; despite being required to let faster cars through, pace delta remained near zero (laps 21‑27), indicating the driver managed back‑marker traffic without losing time.

findings.headline: Temperature drop did not correlate with pace loss
findings.detail: Track temperature fell from 33.0 °C at start to 20.7 °C by lap 30, yet pace delta did not show a systematic slowdown; the best lap in the first Medium stint (92.265 s) occurred on a warm track, while the best lap in the Intermediate stint (97.843 s) was on a cooler, wet track, suggesting temperature alone was not the dominant factor.
